key_insight: Machine-learning forecasts of chaotic bluff-body flow hit a physics-based predictability ceiling that scales with turbulence theory, not just model quality.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a principled way to estimate when ML flow prediction will become unreliable and to design forecasting horizons around intrinsic fluid-dynamics limits.
method: Derived a scaling law for ML forecast deterioration using a Kolmogorov-inspired turbulence framework.
Tested the law on bluff-body flow, a canonical spatiotemporally chaotic fluid system.
Validated the prediction against high-fidelity simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on high-fidelity simulations of bluff-body flow, linking forecast degradation to an analytically derived scaling law.
watch_item: The result is established for bluff-body flow, so transfer to other flow regimes or sensor/ML setups may require re-validation of the scaling law.
paper_title: Turbulence Physics Governs a Scaling Law for the Machine-Learning Predictability Ceiling in Chaotic Flow
